item.title: Ping
item.description:
A simple utility endpoint to check if the API is running.

GET /api/v1/ping.php

  • Description: Checks API health.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "pong",
 "timestamp": "2023-10-27T10:30:00+00:00"
}

item.title: Extensions
item.description:
Retrieves details about currently active extensions.

GET /api/v1/extensions.php

  • Description: Lists active extensions defined in the configuration.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "extensions": [
 {
 "name": "calendar",
 "featherIcon": "calendar"
 },
 {
 "name": "tasks",
 "featherIcon": "check-square"
 }
 ]
 }
}

item.title: Attachments
item.description:
Manages file attachments for notes.

POST /api/v1/attachments.php (Upload)

  • Description: Uploads a new attachment for a note.
  • Request: multipart/form-data
    • note_id (form field): 42
    • attachmentFile (file field): (binary data of my-document.pdf)
  • Response (201 Created): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "id": 101,
 "note_id": 42,
 "name": "my-document.pdf",
 "path": "2023/10/uniqueid_my-document.pdf",
 "type": "application/pdf",
 "size": 123456,
 "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:30:00"
 }
}

POST /api/v1/attachments.php (Delete)

  • Description: Deletes an existing attachment.
  • Request: application/json 
    {
 "_method": "DELETE",
 "id": 101
}
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "deleted_attachment_id": 101
 }
}

GET /api/v1/attachments.php

  • Description: Retrieves a list of attachments, either for a specific note or for all notes with pagination and filtering.
  • Example (By Note ID): GET /api/v1/attachments.php?note_id=42
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": [
 {
 "id": 101,
 "name": "my-document.pdf",
 "path": "2023/10/uniqueid_my-document.pdf",
 "type": "application/pdf",
 "size": 123456,
 "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:30:00",
 "url": "http://localhost/uploads/2023/10/uniqueid_my-document.pdf"
 }
 ]
}

item.title: Operations (write)
item.description:
POST /api/v1/ops.php is the only way to create, change, move or delete notes. The notd frontend uses exactly this endpoint, so anything the UI can do to the outline, a script can do too.

A request carries a list of operations. They are applied in order inside one transaction: either the whole batch is applied or none of it.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/ops.php \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d '{"ops": [
 {"op_id": "demo-1", "type": "create", "id": "0192f6a0-7c3e-7b1a-9f3e-2b1c4d5e6f70",
 "page_id": 87, "parent_id": null, "after": null, "content": "Hello"},
 {"op_id": "demo-2", "type": "edit", "id": "0192f6a0-7c3e-7b1a-9f3e-2b1c4d5e6f70",
 "content": "Hello {status::draft}"}
 ]}'

Operations

Every operation has an op_id (unique string, at most 64 characters), a type and the id of the note it acts on.

item.title: Notes (read)
item.description:
notes.php is read-only. Every change to notes goes through ops.php.

A note looks like this:

{
 "id": "01a1c6b0-ebb1-72da-82de-1d78e583e241",
 "page_id": 87,
 "parent_note_id": null,
 "sort_key": "a0",
 "content": "Project overview {priority::high}",
 "internal": 0,
 "collapsed": 0,
 "active": 1,
 "version": 1,
 "created_at": "2026-11-10 18:20:45",
 "updated_at": "2026-11-10 18:20:45",
 "properties": {
 "priority": [{ "value": "high", "internal": false }]
 },
 "has_attachments": false
}
Field Meaning
id Opaque string, at most 64 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -. New notes get a UUIDv7; notes migrated from older databases keep ids such as "123".
parent_note_id Id of the parent note, or null for a top-level note.
sort_key Position among siblings. Siblings are ordered by (sort_key, id) using plain byte comparison. See Ordering.
version Incremented on every change to the note.
properties Index of the properties found in content, grouped by name. internal is true for weight 3 and above.

GET /api/v1/notes.php?page_id={id}

All notes of a page as a flat list, ordered by sort_key, id. Build the tree from parent_note_id.

item.title: Pages
item.description:
Manages pages, which now also have a content field to drive their properties.

POST /api/v1/pages.php (Create)

  • Description: Creates a new page.
  • Request: application/json 
    {
 "name": "New Project Page",
 "content": "{type::Project}\n{lead:::John Doe}"
}
  • Response (201 Created): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "id": 25,
 "name": "New Project Page",
 "content": "{type::Project}\n{lead:::John Doe}",
 "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:35:00",
 "updated_at": "2023-10-27 10:35:00",
 "properties": {
 "type": [{"value": "Project", "weight": 2, "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:35:00"}],
 "lead": [{"value": "John Doe", "weight": 3, "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:35:00"}]
 }
 }
}

POST /api/v1/pages.php (Update)

  • Description: Updates a page’s name or content.
  • Request: application/json 
    {
 "_method": "PUT",
 "id": 25,
 "content": "{type::Project}\n{lead:::Jane Doe}\n{status::Active}"
}
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "id": 25,
 "name": "New Project Page",
 "content": "{type::Project}\n{lead:::Jane Doe}\n{status::Active}",
 "...": "...",
 "properties": { "..." : "..." }
 }
}

POST /api/v1/pages.php (Delete)

  • Description: Deletes a page and all its associated notes.
  • Request: application/json 
    {
 "_method": "DELETE",
 "id": 25
}
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "deleted_page_id": 25
 }
}

GET /api/v1/pages.php?name={page_name}

  • Description: Retrieves a page by its exact name. If the page does not exist, it will be created with null content.
  • Request example: GET /api/v1/pages.php?name=My%20New%20Page
  • Response example for an existing page (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "id": 26,
 "name": "My New Page",
 "content": "Some existing content.",
 "created_at": "2023-10-28 10:00:00",
 "updated_at": "2023-10-28 10:05:00",
 "properties": {}
 }
}
  • Response example for a newly created page (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "id": 27,
 "name": "My New Page",
 "content": null,
 "created_at": "2023-10-28 10:10:00",
 "updated_at": "2023-10-28 10:10:00",
 "properties": {}
 }
}

GET /api/v1/pages.php?id={id}

  • Description: Retrieves a single page by its ID.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "id": 25,
 "name": "New Project Page",
 "content": "{type::Project}\n{lead:::Jane Doe}\n{status::Active}",
 "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:35:00",
 "updated_at": "2023-10-27 10:40:00",
 "properties": {
 "type": [{"value": "Project", "weight": 2, "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:35:00"}],
 "lead": [{"value": "Jane Doe", "weight": 3, "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:40:00"}],
 "status": [{"value": "Active", "weight": 2, "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:40:00"}]
 }
 }
}

GET /api/v1/pages.php?date={YYYY-MM-DD}

  • Description: Retrieves a list of pages that have a property ‘date’ matching the specified date. The date must be in YYYY-MM-DD format.
  • Request example: GET /api/v1/pages.php?date=2023-11-15
  • Response example (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": [
 {
 "id": 30,
 "name": "Meeting Notes 2023-11-15",
 "content": "Discussed project milestones.\n{date::2023-11-15}",
 "alias": null,
 "updated_at": "2023-11-15 14:00:00"
 },
 {
 "id": 31,
 "name": "Daily Log 2023-11-15",
 "content": "Logged daily activities.\n{date::2023-11-15}",
 "alias": "today-log",
 "updated_at": "2023-11-15 16:30:00"
 }
 ]
}
  • If no pages match the date, an empty array will be returned in the data field. 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": []
}

GET /api/v1/pages.php (List)

  • Description: Retrieves a paginated list of pages.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": [
 {
 "id": 25,
 "name": "New Project Page",
 "content": "...",
 "properties": { "...": "..." }
 }
 ],
 "pagination": { "total_items": 1, "...": "..." }
}

GET /api/v1/child_pages.php?namespace={page_name}

  • Description: Lists the pages directly below a page in the namespace hierarchy. For namespace=Projects this returns Projects/Alpha but not Projects/Alpha/Notes.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": [
 { "id": 12, "name": "Projects/Alpha", "updated_at": "2026-11-10 18:20:45" }
 ]
}

item.title: Append to Page
item.description:
The simplest way for a script to add notes: no ids, no ordering.

POST /api/v1/append_to_page.php

Appends notes at the end of a page. The page is created if it does not exist (a page named like a date, YYYY-MM-DD, becomes a journal page).

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/append_to_page.php \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d '{
 "page_name": "My Project",
 "notes": [
 { "content": "Project overview {priority::high}",
 "children": [ { "content": "TODO Research competitors" } ] },
 { "content": "Second note" }
 ]
 }'
Field Meaning
page_name Required. Name of the page.
notes Required. Either a string (one note) or a list of { "content": "...", "children": [...] } objects. children nest to any depth.

Response (200)

item.title: Properties
item.description:
This endpoint is now read-only. It provides a way to query the Properties table index directly, which can be useful for advanced filtering or finding all entities with a specific property value, without needing to perform a full-text search.

GET /api/v1/properties.php

  • Description: Retrieves all indexed properties for a specific entity.
  • Example Call: GET /api/v1/properties.php?entity_type=note&entity_id=42
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "status": [
 { "id": 201, "value": "TODO", "weight": 2, "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:30:00" },
 { "id": 205, "value": "DONE", "weight": 4, "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:31:00" }
 ],
 "priority": [
 { "id": 202, "value": "High", "weight": 2, "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:30:00" }
 ]
 }
}

item.title: Search
item.description:
Provides powerful search capabilities. It can search by term, find backlinks, list tasks, or list favorited pages.

General Parameters for search types returning notes (e.g., q, backlinks_for_page_name, tasks):

  • include_parent_properties (optional, boolean): Defaults to false. If set to true, each note item in the results array will include a parent_properties field. This field contains an object with aggregated properties from all direct and indirect parent notes. The structure mirrors the main properties field. For search types that do not return notes (e.g., favorites), this parameter has no effect.

GET /api/v1/search.php?q={term}

  • Description: Performs a full-text search across note content. Also supports pagination parameters (page, per_page).
  • Example URL: /api/v1/search.php?q=meeting&include_parent_properties=true
  • Response (200 OK) when include_parent_properties=true: 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "results": [
 {
 "note_id": 42,
 "content": "The full content of the note mentioning the search term.",
 "page_id": 10,
 "page_name": "Project Alpha",
 "content_snippet": "... with the search <mark>term</mark> highlighted ...",
 "properties": { "status": [{"value": "TODO"}] },
 "parent_properties": { "project_code": [{"value": "Alpha"}] }
 }
 ],
 "pagination": { "total_items": 1, "current_page": 1, "per_page": 20, "total_pages": 1 }
 }
}
  • If include_parent_properties is false (default), the parent_properties field will be an empty object ({}) or null.

The Search endpoint also supports other modes:

item.title: Query Notes
item.description:
Runs a SQL query that selects note ids and returns the matching notes. This is what SQL{...} blocks in notes use.

The query runs on a read-only connection. Unless ADVANCED_QUERY_MODE is enabled in the configuration, it must also:

  • start with one of these forms:
    • SELECT id FROM Notes WHERE ...
    • SELECT [DISTINCT] N.id FROM Notes N JOIN Properties P ON N.id = P.note_id WHERE ...
    • SELECT id FROM Notes WHERE id IN (SELECT note_id FROM Properties WHERE ...
  • contain no semicolon and none of the words INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, TRUNCATE, ALTER, EXEC, CREATE, ATTACH, DETACH;
  • only refer to these columns when using a table prefix: id, content, page_id, parent_note_id, created_at, updated_at, sort_key, version, collapsed, active (Notes) and note_id, name, value, weight (Properties).

The first selected column must be the note id. Do not add LIMIT; use page and per_page.

item.title: Templates
item.description:
Manages reusable templates for creating notes and pages.

POST /api/v1/templates.php (Create)

  • Description: Creates a new template.
  • Request: application/json 
    {
 "_method": "POST",
 "type": "note",
 "name": "daily-review",
 "content": "## Daily Review\n\n### What went well?\n\n- \n\n### What could be improved?\n\n- "
}
  • Response (201 Created): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "message": "Template created successfully"
 }
}

GET /api/v1/templates.php?type=note

  • Description: Retrieves all available templates of a given type.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": [
 {
 "name": "daily-review",
 "content": "## Daily Review\n\n### What went well?\n\n- \n\n### What could be improved?\n\n- "
 }
 ]
}

item.title: Webhooks
item.description:
Manages webhook subscriptions. A webhook is an HTTP POST that notd sends to a URL of your choice when a property changes.

  • Deliveries are sent after the change has been saved, never while the database is locked, and not at all if the change was rolled back.
  • Only verified and active webhooks receive events: call the verify action once after creating a webhook.
  • Each delivery carries the headers X-Notd-Event and X-Notd-Signature (HMAC-SHA256 of the body with the webhook’s secret).
  • PUT and DELETE can also be sent as POST with "_method": "PUT" or "_method": "DELETE" in the JSON body.
  • Set WEBHOOKS_ENABLED to false in the configuration to stop all deliveries.

POST /api/v1/webhooks.php (Create)

  • Description: Registers a new webhook.
  • Request: application/json 
    {
 "url": "https://example.com/webhook-receiver",
 "entity_type": "note",
 "property_names": ["status", "priority"],
 "event_types": ["property_change", "entity_created"]
}
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "id": 1,
 "url": "https://example.com/webhook-receiver",
 "entity_type": "note",
 "property_names": ["status", "priority"],
 "event_types": ["property_change", "entity_created"],
 "secret": "whsec_... (only shown on creation)",
 "...": "..."
 }
}

POST /api/v1/webhooks.php?action=test&id=1

  • Description: Sends a test event to the specified webhook.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "message": "Test event sent. Check history for result."
 }
}

GET /api/v1/webhooks.php?action=history&id=1

  • Description: Retrieves the delivery history for a webhook.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "pagination": { "total": 1, "page": 1, "limit": 20 },
 "history": [
 {
 "id": 1,
 "webhook_id": 1,
 "event_type": "test",
 "payload": "{\"event\":\"test\",...}",
 "response_code": 200,
 "response_body": "{\"status\":\"ok\"}",
 "success": 1,
 "created_at": "2023-10-27 11:00:00"
 }
 ]
 }
}

GET /api/v1/webhooks.php (List)

  • Description: Lists all configured webhooks.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": [
 {
 "id": 1,
 "url": "https://example.com/webhook-receiver",
 "entity_type": "note",
 "property_names": ["status", "priority"],
 "event_types": ["property_change", "entity_created"],
 "active": 1,
 "verified": 1,
 "last_triggered": "2023-10-27 11:00:00"
 }
 ]
}
